farkle_frenzy_revision_prompt.purpose:
Refine and stabilize the existing Farkle Frenzy implementation while preserving all canonical gameplay systems from the master architecture document.
This revision focuses on: - tray-based chain capacity logic - delayed scoring/energy burn mechanics - visual readability - improved cube dice rendering - refined bomb presentation - dynamic lighting - strategic visibility tradeoffs - board layout fixes - chain validation bug fixes - bomb spawn balancing

tray_system.overview:
Replace the current instant-resolution chain behavior with a physical tray-processing system.
The tray becomes a visible gameplay mechanic and directly controls: - chain capacity - scoring timing - energy timing - player decision-making - board readability pressure

tray_behavior.capacity_rules:
The player may only create a chain equal to the number of currently empty tray slots.
Example: - 6 empty slots = max chain length 6 - 3 empty slots = max chain length 3 - 1 empty slot = max chain length 1
Tray occupancy dynamically limits selectable chain length.

object_flow.green_energy_spheres: When clicked: - smoothly fall into tray - shrink during fall - occupy tray slot - remain temporarily - burn off after delay - disappear from tray - award player energy only AFTER burn completion
object_flow.dice_chains: Any committed chain: - scoring or non-scoring - drops physically into tray - shrinks during movement - occupies slots - waits before processing - burns off after delay - disappears from tray - awards score only AFTER burn completion

burn_behavior.effects: - gradual dissolve - ember fade - particle ash - opacity reduction - soft glow decay
burn_behavior.completion: After burn completion: - object removed from tray - slot becomes available - remaining tray objects smoothly shift left

tray_behavior.strategic_goal:
This system intentionally creates timing-based strategic pressure.
Players must decide: - collect energy spheres and wait for tray clearing OR - immediately commit smaller chains
Collecting too many energy spheres reduces tray space and slows future chain capacity.
Energy collection becomes both: - a reward - a temporary gameplay tax

chain_validation.critical_bug:
A bug currently allows players to exceed the intended six-tile chain limit by rapidly dragging across the board.
The visuals fail to display the illegal chain length properly, but the underlying logic still accepts chains longer than six.
chain_validation.required_fix:
Hard-cap chain length at six tiles in BOTH: - visual layer - gameplay logic layer
Once six tiles are selected: - all additional tiles become non-interactable - further drag movement ignored - no hidden overflow chains allowed

dice_visual_upgrade.geometry:
Replace current flattened rectangular prism dice with proper full cubes.
Dice must visually resemble authentic casino dice.

faces.pips:
Every face must contain proper pip layouts.
Examples: - face 1 = single center pip - face 2 = diagonal pair - face 3 = triangle arrangement - face 4 = four corners - face 5 = four corners + center - face 6 = three vertical pairs
faces.rules: - pips visible on all exposed faces - maintain existing color coding - preserve readability during movement - support lighting/reflection

special_tiles.icons:
Replace temporary/pixelated special icons with refined high-resolution symbolic overlays inspired by lobby visuals.
Applies to: - Wild - Ice - Stone - Lock - other special entities

rainbow_bomb_revision.goal: Make Rainbow Bomb detonations feel dramatic, suspenseful, magical, and visually overwhelming.

spawn_rules.skill_spawns: Preserve canonical spawning: - Straight chains spawn Rainbow Bombs - Six-of-a-kind spawns Standard Bombs
spawn_rules.random_spawns:
Preserve accidental/random bomb spawning behavior caused by current systems.
DO NOT remove random bomb appearances entirely.
Instead: - reduce frequency substantially - make random bomb spawns feel rare - preserve surprise factor

anticipation_phase.behavior: - slow suspense buildup - rainbow cycling intensifies - audio charge-up - subtle board dimming - player anticipation moment

detonation.screen_effects: - gray/desaturate entire board - preserve chosen target color vibrancy - selected color dominates screen
detonation.tile_feedback: Matching tiles: - glow intensely - pulse brightly - become unmistakably visible - clearly communicate destruction targets
detonation.visual_style: - far more rainbow energy - magical spectrum explosions - layered rainbow particles - soft bloom - elegant rather than violent

board_layout_revision.issue: On the standard 7x7 board: - left and right edge columns visually clip offscreen - physics and spacing currently distort presentation
board_layout_revision.required_fix:
DO NOT reduce cube size.
Instead: - adjust spacing/alignment - compress column padding slightly - reposition overall board - increase vertical board positioning - ensure all edge columns fully visible

bomb_lighting.standard_bomb:
Explosion should emit actual dynamic light.
Include: - radial flash - environmental lighting pulse - glow falloff - brief board illumination
bomb_lighting.rainbow_bomb: Generate: - spectrum lighting - layered rainbow bloom - full-screen color atmosphere

energy_spheres.appearance: Make energy spheres emit bright neon green light.
energy_spheres.dynamic_glow: Glow should: - radiate outward - softly illuminate nearby tiles - pulse organically - react to movement physics - feel alive
energy_spheres.strategic_visibility:
Leaving spheres on the board: - improves visibility - keeps board illuminated
Collecting spheres: - removes local lighting - darkens board sections - slightly reduces readability
This intentionally creates another strategic layer: visibility versus energy acquisition.

desired_player_feeling.gameplay: - high skill ceiling - meaningful timing decisions - tactical board reading - satisfying chain management
desired_player_feeling.visuals: - casino-grade polish - rich neon atmosphere - readable chaos - dynamic lighting - magical spectacle
desired_player_feeling.overall_identity: Farkle Frenzy should feel like: - a living puzzle organism - a risk/reward casino strategy game - a reactive neon physics playground - a skill-first arcade experience
